title: Introduce RAG Slate: lightweight multimodal RAG playground and toolchain quickstart
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a compact multimodal RAG quickstart (images + text) with a lightweight web playground, devcontainer, and structured tool-binding examples for local testing and telemetry.
description: Motivation: Teams frequently ask for compact local-first examples that show how to combine text retrieval with image grounding and lightweight tool-calling. RAG Slate is a minimal, opinionated quickstart that demonstrates: 1) multimodal retrieval (text + image captions/embeddings), 2) a small browser-based playground for stepwise interaction and streaming outputs, 3) an example image-annotation tool bound to the agent via a simple HTTP shim, and 4) an instrumentation recipe for lightweight telemetry and structured output validation. This PR introduces the quickstart, docs, and examples used in our workshop track. Checklist: - [x] Add quickstart repo layout, README and devcontainer for zero-setup local run - [x] Implement a tiny web playground (React) that streams incremental tokens and inline images - [x] Provide an image-annotation tool stub (python/fastapi) and a wasm shim for browser dev - [x] Add structured output schema and JSON schema validator used in postprocessing - [x] Add telemetry probe config (trace/span names + example metrics) - [x] Add scripted smoke CI job that runs the quickstart locally in the devcontainer and exercises retrieval+toolcall flow What changed (high level): - quickstarts/rag-slate: new directory with README, architecture.md, devcontainer config, and compact example datasets (small text index + 30 sample images). - quickstarts/rag-slate/playground: minimal React app demonstrating streaming generation, stepwise retrieval inspector, and an image viewer that highlights retrieved passages anchored to image captions. - quickstarts/rag-slate/tools/image-annotator: tiny FastAPI service (POST /annotate) that returns bounding boxes and labels; used to demonstrate tool-calling and structured tool responses. - quickstarts/rag-slate/dev: wasm-proxy binary stub + docker-compose for local mode (allows running browser + annotator + local index). - docs/site: added a short quickstart guide and an architecture diagram referencing the new playground and tool-binding examples. Testing notes: - Local smoke tested in devcontainer on Mac M1 and Ubuntu CI runner (arm and x86) - CI: new job quickstart-smoke that starts docker-compose, seeds index, runs E2E smoke script (generates a short conversation, triggers image annotation, validates structured output). The job flaky once due to network pull timeouts; added a retry wrapper and improved image caching. Rollout plan: - Merge to main and publish quickstart on docs site under "Quickstarts > RAG" - Announce in weekly digest and add a short tutorial session for Developer Advocate workshop next week - Monitor telemetry in the first 48h for unexpected errors or high latency (span: rag_slate.query, rag_slate.toolcall) Related work: ENG-5382 (multimodal retrieval experiments), PM-214 (quickstart roadmap). Notes for reviewers: focus on the devcontainer reproducibility and the structured schema for tool output; the playground is intentionally minimal and meant as a reference implementation rather than production code.

review_thread: Carlos Mendes (reviewer): The streaming implementation is neat. Can we ensure token chunks are capped to avoid layout thrash in the playground?
Priya Kapoor (author): Good catch — added a 120ms debounce and a 256-token chunk cap in the client; included note in architecture.md.
Aisha Thompson (reviewer): The JSON schema for tool output looks fine, but add an example of a failed tool response and how the agent falls back.
Priya Kapoor (author): Added a 'tool_error' variant to the schema and a small handler in the playground that shows structured error messages and suggests fallback text.
Liam Nguyen (reviewer): CI job passed locally for me; one nit: rename docker-compose service 'annotator' -> 'image-annotator' for clarity.
Priya Kapoor (author): Renamed service, updated docs and compose file. Ready for merge.
Carlos Mendes (approver): Approved — small, self-contained quickstart that aligns with the RAG docs taxonomy.
